title: A contract platform that turned days of work into minutes
summary: An end-to-end contract management platform: SPFx front end, Azure Functions reading live sales data from the internal data warehouse, Key Vault, Entra ID and DocuSign e-signature — built on systems the company already owned.
before: Turning margin contribution into a contract took several days.
The live sales data the process depended on sat in an internal Azure SQL data warehouse, on premises.
Contracts needed e-signature without exposing signing credentials, and in line with Saudi PDPL data-residency rules.
A firewall subnet-allowlisting gap blocked the Azure Function App from reaching the data warehouse at all.
work: Built the front end in SPFx (React, TypeScript) inside SharePoint.
Connected it to the internal Azure SQL data warehouse through an Azure Function App, so contracts use live sales data.
Kept every credential in Azure Key Vault and authenticated users with Entra ID.
Integrated DocuSign through an Azure Function credential-broker pattern, so signing credentials never leave the server.
Diagnosed the Azure-to-on-premises networking failure, closed the firewall allowlisting gap and verified secure connectivity.
outcome: Contract processing cut from several days to minutes.
28 ms end-to-end response.
Built on systems the company already owned.
Approved at Chief Officer and Director level.

title: Retiring InfoPath: 8 forms rebuilt for 500+ users
summary: Eight legacy InfoPath forms rebuilt into production SharePoint ahead of Microsoft's retirement deadline, used by 500+ people across 15 departments.
before: Day-to-day processes ran on InfoPath forms, a product Microsoft has retired.
There was a hard end-of-support deadline: no fixes, no new features after it.
The forms served 500+ users across 15 departments, so a failure would hit the whole company.
work: Rebuilt each of the 8 InfoPath forms in modern SharePoint.
Moved the approvals and notifications behind them to Power Automate.
Switched departments over in stages so work didn't stop.
outcome: All 8 forms live in production SharePoint before the deadline.
500+ users across 15 departments moved off InfoPath.

title: An internal audit platform, from requirements to production
result: 12/12 UAT cases passed, zero deployment issues
summary: A platform for raising, tracking and closing internal audit observations, with tiered reminders, overdue escalation and structured export — delivered from requirements to production and still owned after go-live.
before: Internal Audit needed one place to raise, track and close observations.
Owners needed reminders, with escalation when items went overdue.
Audit needed structured exports for reporting.
work: Gathered requirements with Internal Audit and designed the solution.
Built tiered reminders with overdue escalation, and structured export.
Wrote and ran 12 scripted UAT cases before go-live.
Kept ownership after go-live.
outcome: All 12 scripted UAT cases passed.
Deployed to production with zero deployment issues.
Still running and supported after go-live.

title: Rebuilding a failed CAPEX approval workflow
result: Failed workflow replaced, multi-tier approvals live
summary: Finance's CAPEX request system rebuilt on modern SharePoint with a multi-tier approval hierarchy, replacing a SharePoint Designer workflow that had failed.
before: Capital expenditure requests ran on a SharePoint Designer workflow that had failed.
SharePoint Designer workflows are a retired technology, so patching it was not an option.
Requests needed to pass through several levels of approval.
work: Rebuilt the CAPEX request system on modern SharePoint.
Designed a multi-tier approval hierarchy to match how Finance signs off spend.
outcome: Failed SharePoint Designer workflow retired.
CAPEX requests running on modern SharePoint with multi-tier approvals.

title: 45,000 documents across four companies, with zero loss
summary: A group-wide migration of 45,000+ documents (~60 GB) across four legal entities, reorganised and reconciled file by file.
before: Documents for four legal entities in the group needed to be moved and reorganised.
At around 60 GB and 45,000+ files, a silent loss would be easy to miss.
work: Planned and executed the migration across all four legal entities.
Reorganised the content into the new structure.
Reconciled source against destination to verify every document arrived.
outcome: 45,000+ documents (~60 GB) migrated.
Verified reconciliation with zero loss.

title: Automating vendor invoice posting into Dynamics 365
summary: A Power Platform integration that posts vendor invoices into Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations, with duplicate prevention, retry logic and error alerts in Teams.
before: Vendor invoices had to be posted into Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations.
Any automation had to make sure the same invoice could never be posted twice.
Failed postings needed to be retried and seen by someone, not lost.
work: Built the Power Platform to Dynamics 365 F&O integration.
Added duplicate prevention.
Added retry logic for failed postings.
Sent errors to Microsoft Teams so the team sees them straight away.
outcome: Vendor invoice posting automated.
Duplicate postings prevented.
Failures retried automatically and alerted in Teams.

title: A permission audit framework and tenant hardening for five companies
result: Repeatable permission audits, CA and DLP baselines
summary: A PowerShell/CSOM framework for auditing SharePoint permissions across five group companies, alongside Conditional Access and DLP hardening of the Microsoft 365 tenant.
before: Five group companies shared one Microsoft 365 environment.
There was no repeatable way to audit who had access to what.
The tenant needed Conditional Access and data-loss-prevention baselines.
work: Built a PowerShell/CSOM permission audit and governance framework.
Led Microsoft 365 security hardening, including Conditional Access.
Put DLP policies in place.
outcome: Permission audits are repeatable instead of manual.
Conditional Access and DLP baselines in place across the tenant.

title: Closing an external sharing leak in SharePoint Online
result: All unauthorised access removed within 48 hours
summary: After a live security incident, I audited the client's Microsoft 365 tenant, removed every unauthorised external share across SharePoint and OneDrive, and tightened governance so it couldn't happen again.
situation: An external sharing setting in SharePoint Online had been left too open. Sensitive internal documents were reachable by users at a Canadian partner organisation, and the exposure ran across several site collections.
Nobody knew exactly how far it went. The first job was to find out — quickly — and stop it.
work: Audited the whole tenant with PowerShell and the Microsoft 365 admin center.
Listed every externally shared link, guest account and anonymous access link.
Revoked access in a controlled order so business-critical sharing wasn't broken by accident.
Reset sharing policy at both tenant and site-collection level.
Added monitoring alerts and Conditional Access rules to catch drift early.
outcome: 100% of unauthorised external access removed within 48 hours.
Sharing policy tightened and enforced with Conditional Access.
Incident report delivered to stakeholders.
No recurrence since the fix.
before: Tenant-level external sharing was set far too open.
Sensitive internal documents in SharePoint and OneDrive were reachable by users at a partner organisation.
The exposure ran across several site collections, not just one.
Old sharing links, guest accounts and anonymous links had piled up with nobody reviewing them.
No alerting existed to catch over-sharing when it happened.

title: Moving 5,000 people from Google Workspace to Microsoft 365
summary: Drive, Shared Drives, Sites, Gmail and Groups — the whole Google workplace moved to Microsoft 365 inside six months, with a tracking app so everyone could see where each workload stood.
situation: A large enterprise wanted off Google Workspace entirely: Drive, Shared Drives, Google Sites, Gmail and Groups. The deadline was six months and the business couldn't stop working while it happened.
work: Ran a pre-migration assessment and mapped every source to its destination.
Moved Google Drive and Shared Drives to SharePoint, and Google Sites to SharePoint (classic and modern).
Moved Gmail to Exchange Online, and Google Groups to Microsoft 365 Groups and Teams.
Used ShareGate, AvePoint, Cloudiway and Microsoft Migration Manager, with delta syncs before cutover.
Built a tracking app so the team could follow every workload, then validated everything after migration.
outcome: 5,000+ users migrated within the six-month window.
Cutover completed with zero data loss.
Replaced the client's legacy Google Sheets workflows with a governed SharePoint application after go-live.
before: The whole workplace was split across Google Drive, Shared Drives, Sites, Gmail and Groups.
Day-to-day processes ran on Google Sheets with no governance or audit trail.
A hard six-month deadline, and the business could not stop working during the move.
No single view of migration progress across workloads.

title: A C# platform for automated tenant-to-tenant migration
summary: An internal C# console platform that automates Microsoft 365 tenant-to-tenant data migration through Google Cloud and Microsoft service-account APIs.
before: Tenant-to-tenant data moves needed to be automated.
Transfers had to run at scale without handing out user credentials.
work: Designed and built a C# console platform.
Used Google Cloud and Microsoft service-account APIs so transfers run without user credentials.
Automated the transfer end to end.
outcome: Credential-secure, automated tenant-to-tenant transfer at scale.

title: A Copilot-assisted risk management module at EY GDS
summary: I led the Risk Management module, using Microsoft Copilot for AI-assisted release analysis and approval orchestration, alongside 10+ Power Apps and 50+ Power Automate workflows for internal operations.
work: Led the Risk Management module, integrating Microsoft Copilot for AI-assisted release analysis and approval orchestration.
Used Microsoft Graph and REST APIs to surface organisational context inside the approval workflow.
Built 10+ Power Apps canvas applications with 50+ Power Automate workflows, with data validation and error handling.
Hardened Microsoft 365 security across Outlook, SharePoint and Azure AD, and automated admin and reporting with PowerShell.
Worked in Agile/Scrum with global stakeholders: requirements, documentation, UAT and production support.
outcome: Risk Management module delivered with AI-assisted analysis.
10+ apps and 50+ workflows in production.
Delivered through formal change control with zero compliance breaches.
before: Releases needed risk analysis and a controlled approval process.
Approvers needed organisational context in front of them when deciding.
Internal processes — leave, resource allocation, onboarding — needed proper applications.
Everything had to meet EY's security and change-management standards.

title: Stabilising 14 SharePoint on-prem apps for a US logistics company
summary: Expense, accident-report and approval apps on an ageing SharePoint farm were creating duplicate records every day. I found the race conditions, fixed 50+ broken workflows and rebuilt the Accident Report app from scratch.
situation: WARD ran 14+ business-critical applications — expenses, accident reports, approvals — on an ageing SharePoint on-premises environment.
Forms were creating duplicate entries, the sequential ID generators kept breaking, and an unstable Node setup made every fix risky. Staff felt it every day.
work: Traced the duplicates to front-end race conditions when two people submitted at the same time, and fixed them.
Upgraded the Node versions the apps depended on.
Rebuilt the Accident Report application end-to-end with a new UI and a reliable back end.
Fixed 50+ SharePoint Designer workflows across the portfolio.
outcome: All 14+ applications stable.
Zero duplicate submissions after the fix.
New Accident Report application live in production.
before: Forms created duplicate records whenever two people submitted at the same time (a front-end race condition).
Sequential ID generators kept breaking, so records lost their reference numbers.
Unstable, outdated Node versions made every fix risky.
50+ SharePoint Designer workflows were failing across the app portfolio.
The Accident Report app was too unreliable to patch and had to be rebuilt.

title: 20+ applications across six client engagements
summary: Incident reporting, expense, leave and credit trackers, real-time web parts and a training management system — 20+ applications for clients in the US, UK and Canada, running six engagements at once.
before: Clients needed incident reporting and tracking, and expense, leave and credit requests with multi-stage approvals.
Intranets needed live data from external systems.
Some clients were still on legacy platforms and needed to move to SharePoint Online without disrupting the business.
work: Built SPFx incident reporting and tracking systems.
Built integrated expense, leave and credit tracker suites with multi-stage approval routing.
Built real-time web parts consuming external REST APIs, and a React/Node.js training management system integrated with SharePoint.
Led legacy-to-SharePoint Online migrations and built branded intranet portals.
Supported pre-sales with effort estimates, solution proposals and technical documentation.
outcome: 20+ applications delivered across 6+ concurrent engagements.
Clients in the US, UK and Canada.

title: World-clock and weather web parts for a Dubai intranet
summary: Custom SPFx web parts — a multi-timezone world clock and calendar, and a live regional weather panel — for a modern SharePoint intranet serving staff across several countries.
situation: A large food company in Dubai wanted its modern SharePoint intranet to be useful to staff spread across several countries. They needed live, local information that SharePoint doesn't provide out of the box.
work: Built custom SPFx web parts in React and TypeScript.
A world clock and calendar web part covering every office time zone.
A live weather web part with region-specific data pulled from REST APIs.
outcome: Web parts delivered and live on the intranet.
Better intranet engagement from international staff across multiple offices.
before: Staff were spread across offices in several countries and time zones.
SharePoint’s out-of-the-box web parts had no world clock, multi-zone calendar or live local weather.
The intranet needed to feel useful day to day, not just be a document store.

title: An internal AI assistant on Azure OpenAI and SharePoint
summary: A GenAI assistant that searches SharePoint content and handles routine requests for several departments, built with Azure OpenAI, Copilot APIs and an SPFx front end.
situation: Several departments were spending time answering the same questions and processing the same standard requests, and finding documents in SharePoint wasn't easy.
work: Designing the assistant around Azure OpenAI and Microsoft 365 Copilot APIs, with an SPFx interface inside SharePoint.
Running alongside it: a standalone Security Guard application and a Freshworks ITSM integration that creates tickets automatically.
outcome: R&D phase complete.
Proof of concept live for 2 departments.
Production rollout under way, with more departments planned.
before: Several departments spent hours answering the same questions again and again.
Standard requests were processed by hand.
Finding the right document in SharePoint was slow.
